questions.q: Which law is known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012?
questions.e: R.A. 10175 is the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012.

questions.q: Which law is known as the Data Privacy Act of 2012?
questions.e: R.A. 10173 is the Data Privacy Act of 2012.

questions.q: Which law is the Anti-Child Pornography Act of 2009?
questions.e: R.A. 9775 is the Anti-Child Pornography Act of 2009.

questions.q: Which law is the Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009?
questions.e: R.A. 9995 addresses photo and video voyeurism.

questions.q: Which law created the Department of Information and Communications Technology?
questions.e: R.A. 10844 is the DICT Act of 2015.

questions.q: In what year was the Cybercrime Prevention Act signed into law?
questions.e: R.A. 10175 was signed in 2012.

questions.q: Which agency was created by the Data Privacy Act of 2012?
o: Department of Information and Communications Technology
questions.e: R.A. 10173 created the National Privacy Commission.

questions.q: What is the main focus of R.A. 10173?
o: Protecting individual personal information in information and communications systems
questions.e: The Data Privacy Act protects personal information.

questions.q: What is the main focus of R.A. 10175?
questions.e: The Cybercrime Prevention Act punishes cybercrimes.

questions.q: A person accesses a company server without authorization. Which law is most directly applicable?
questions.e: Illegal access is a cybercrime under R.A. 10175.

questions.q: A school leaks students' grades and addresses to the public. Which law is most directly applicable?
questions.e: Unlawful processing and disclosure of personal data falls under the Data Privacy Act.

questions.q: A website distributes sexual images of a minor. Which law is most directly applicable?
questions.e: Child pornography is covered by the Anti-Child Pornography Act.

questions.q: A person secretly records a coworker in a private room and posts the video online. Which law is most directly applicable?
questions.e: Secret recording of a private area violates the Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act.

questions.q: Which agency was created to be the primary policy and planning body for ICT in the Philippines?
questions.e: The DICT is the primary ICT policy agency created by R.A. 10844.

questions.q: Which is an offense under R.A. 10175?
questions.e: Illegal access to a computer system is a cybercrime.

questions.q: Which cybercrime involves intercepting a non-public transmission of computer data without right?
questions.e: Illegal interception captures non-public data transmissions.

questions.q: Which cybercrime involves altering, damaging, or deleting data without right?
questions.e: Data interference covers unauthorized alteration or deletion of data.

questions.q: Which cybercrime involves hindering the functioning of a computer or network without right?
questions.e: System interference disrupts system functioning.

questions.q: Which cybercrime involves producing or distributing tools designed to commit cybercrimes?
questions.e: Misuse of devices covers tools, passwords, and programs used for cybercrime.

questions.q: What is cybersquatting?
o: Acquiring a domain name in bad faith to profit or harm another
questions.e: Cybersquatting is bad-faith domain name acquisition.

questions.q: Which is a computer-related offense under R.A. 10175?
questions.e: Identity theft through computer systems is a computer-related offense.

questions.q: A person uses another person's name and passwords online to obtain a loan. This is which offense?
questions.e: Using identifying information to obtain a benefit is identity theft.

questions.q: Which content-related offense involves paid sexual acts performed with a computer?
questions.e: Cybersex under R.A. 10175 involves lascivious acts for favor or consideration.

questions.q: Unsolicited commercial communications are commonly known as what?
questions.e: Unsolicited commercial communications are spam.

questions.q: Which offense is explicitly included in R.A. 10175 as a cybercrime?
questions.e: R.A. 10175 lists libel committed through a computer system.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a cybercrime offense under R.A. 10175?
questions.e: Illegal parking is unrelated to cybercrime.

questions.q: R.A. 10175 gives special protection to systems vital to national security. These are called what?
questions.e: Critical infrastructure receives higher protection under the law.

questions.q: Collecting traffic data in real time under R.A. 10175 generally requires what?
o: Consent from the ISP owner only
Due cause and a court order
questions.e: Real-time traffic data collection needs due cause and a court order.

questions.q: What level of authorization is needed to collect the content of communications?
questions.e: Content requires a warrant; traffic data may be collected with a court order.

questions.q: How long is a preservation order for computer data generally effective under R.A. 10175?
questions.e: Preservation orders run for six months and may be extended.

questions.q: Which body is the lead agency for coordinating cybercrime investigations under R.A. 10175?
questions.e: The CICC coordinates cybercrime investigation and prevention.

questions.q: Which office under the Department of Justice handles cybercrime matters?
questions.e: The DOJ Office of Cybercrime is designated by R.A. 10175.

questions.q: Which law applies to crimes defined in the Revised Penal Code when committed through information and communications technology?
questions.e: R.A. 10175 covers RPC crimes committed through ICT.

questions.q: Which right allows a data subject to know how their personal data is being processed?
questions.e: The right to be informed covers processing details.

questions.q: Which right allows a data subject to refuse further processing of their data?
questions.e: Data subjects may object to processing.

questions.q: Which right allows a data subject to view the personal data held about them?
questions.e: The right to access allows viewing of one's data.

questions.q: Which right allows a data subject to correct inaccurate information?
questions.e: Rectification corrects inaccurate or incomplete data.

questions.q: Which right allows a data subject to request blocking or removal of data?
questions.e: Erasure or blocking removes or suspends processing of data.

questions.q: Which right allows a data subject to claim compensation for harm caused by data misuse?
questions.e: The right to damages provides compensation.

questions.q: Which right allows a data subject to move their data to another service provider?
questions.e: Portability allows electronic transfer of data to another controller.

questions.q: Which right allows a data subject to bring a grievance before the NPC?
questions.e: Data subjects may file complaints with the NPC.

questions.q: Which of the following is sensitive personal information?
questions.e: Health, religion, ethnicity, and similar data are sensitive personal information.

questions.q: Which best defines processing of personal information?
o: Any operation on personal data such as collection, storage, use, or destruction
questions.e: Processing covers the whole data lifecycle.

questions.q: What is the difference between a personal information controller and a processor?
o: The controller decides how data is processed; the processor acts on the controller's behalf
The processor owns the data; the controller only stores it
The controller is the data subject
questions.e: Controllers decide processing; processors execute on their behalf.

questions.q: Consent under R.A. 10173 must be what?
o: Given only in writing by a lawyer
questions.e: Valid consent must be freely given, specific, and informed.

questions.q: Within how many hours must a personal data breach generally be reported to the NPC?
questions.e: The IRR provides for notification within 72 hours.

questions.q: Who is responsible for ensuring an organization complies with the Data Privacy Act?
questions.e: A DPO oversees data privacy compliance.

questions.q: Under R.A. 9775, a child is a person below what age?
questions.e: The law defines a child as below 18 years old.

questions.q: Which medium is covered by R.A. 9775?
o: Electronic, mechanical, digital, optical, and other means
questions.e: Child pornography includes representations through any medium.

questions.q: What duty do internet service providers have under R.A. 9775?
o: Install blocking or filtering software and notify authorities of violations
questions.e: ISPs must block or filter child pornography and report violations.

questions.q: Under R.A. 9995, what is a private area?
o: Naked or undergarment-clad genitals, buttocks, or breasts under circumstances of reasonable privacy
questions.e: The law defines private areas and privacy expectations.

questions.q: What key element must be present for photo or video voyeurism under R.A. 9995?
o: Lack of consent and a reasonable expectation of privacy
A public place and a crowd
questions.e: Secret capture in a private setting is central to the offense.

questions.q: Which act is prohibited by R.A. 9995?
o: Filming yourself and keeping it private
Taking a photo with consent in public
Broadcasting or sharing a secretly recorded private video
questions.e: Sharing or broadcasting voyeuristic recordings is prohibited.

questions.q: What is the penalty range under R.A. 9995?
o: 3 to 7 years imprisonment and a fine of P100,000 to P500,000
questions.e: The law imposes 3-7 years and a fine of P100,000-P500,000.

questions.q: Which law would apply to a person who uses a phone to secretly film someone undressing in a private room?
questions.e: Secret filming of a private area is photo/video voyeurism.

questions.q: Which law applies to an online store that sells photos of abused children?
questions.e: Child pornography is covered by R.A. 9775.

questions.q: Which law applies to a bank that fails to protect customers' personal information?
questions.e: The Data Privacy Act governs personal information protection.

questions.q: Which law applies to a hacker who steals a user's login credentials?
questions.e: Hacking and illegal access are cybercrimes under R.A. 10175.

questions.q: Which law applies to spam messages sent without consent?
questions.e: Unsolicited commercial communications are covered by the Cybercrime Act.

questions.q: Which law is the legal basis for the National Privacy Commission?
questions.e: The NPC was created by the Data Privacy Act.

questions.q: Which Republic Act is known as the Cybercrime Prevention Act of 2012?
questions.e: R.A. 10175 is the Cybercrime Prevention Act.

questions.q: Which Republic Act is known as the Data Privacy Act of 2012?
questions.e: R.A. 10173 is the Data Privacy Act.

questions.q: Which Republic Act is the Anti-Child Pornography Act of 2009?
questions.e: R.A. 9775 is the Anti-Child Pornography Act.

questions.q: Which Republic Act is the Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act of 2009?
questions.e: R.A. 9995 is the Anti-Photo and Video Voyeurism Act.

questions.q: Which Republic Act created the Department of Information and Communications Technology?
questions.e: R.A. 10844 is the DICT Act of 2015.

questions.q: Which agency was created by the Data Privacy Act of 2012?
questions.e: The NPC enforces the Data Privacy Act.

questions.q: Which body coordinates the investigation and prevention of cybercrime?
questions.e: The CICC is the cybercrime coordination body.

questions.q: Which office under the DOJ is designated to handle cybercrime cases?
questions.e: The DOJ Office of Cybercrime handles cybercrime matters.

questions.q: What is the bad-faith acquisition of a domain name to profit or harm another called?
questions.e: Cybersquatting is a cybercrime offense.

questions.q: What cybercrime involves access to a computer system without right?
questions.e: Illegal access is the legal term for unauthorized system access.

questions.q: What cybercrime involves the interception of non-public computer data transmissions?
questions.e: Illegal interception targets non-public transmissions.

questions.q: What cybercrime involves unauthorized alteration or deletion of computer data?
questions.e: Data interference covers altering, damaging, or deleting data.

questions.q: What cybercrime involves hindering the functioning of a computer or network?
questions.e: System interference disrupts operations.

questions.q: What cybercrime involves producing or distributing tools for committing cybercrimes?
questions.e: Misuse of devices covers cybercrime tools and passwords.

questions.q: Which data subject right allows personal data to be moved to another service?
questions.e: Portability enables transfer between providers.

questions.q: Which data subject right allows correction of inaccurate information?
questions.e: Rectification corrects inaccurate data.

questions.q: Which data subject right allows the removal or blocking of personal data?
questions.e: Erasure or blocking removes or suspends data processing.

questions.q: What do we call the individual whose personal information is processed?
questions.e: The data subject is the person the data belongs to.

questions.q: What do we call the organization that controls or decides how personal data is processed?
questions.e: The controller determines the purpose and means of processing.

questions.q: What do we call the organization that processes data on behalf of another?
questions.e: Processors act on behalf of controllers.

questions.q: To which agency must a personal data breach generally be reported within 72 hours?
questions.e: Breach notification goes to the NPC.

questions.q: What inter-agency body was created under R.A. 9775?
questions.e: R.A. 9775 created the IACACP.

questions.q: What is the offense of secretly capturing a person's private area without consent called?
questions.e: R.A. 9995 punishes photo and video voyeurism.

questions.q: What is the legal term for unsolicited commercial communications?
questions.e: Spam is the common term.

questions.q: What does CICC stand for?
questions.e: CICC is the Cybercrime Investigation and Coordination Center.

questions.q: R.A. 10175 is the [[Data Privacy Act]] of 2012.
questions.e: R.A. 10175 is the Cybercrime Prevention Act; R.A. 10173 is the Data Privacy Act.

questions.q: R.A. 10173 created the National Privacy Commission.
questions.e: The NPC is created by the Data Privacy Act.

questions.q: R.A. 9775 protects children from pornography and exploitation.
questions.e: The law defines and punishes child pornography.

questions.q: R.A. 9995 [[allows]] secret recording of people in private places.
questions.e: The law prohibits secret recording in private settings.

questions.q: R.A. 10844 created the Department of Information and Communications Technology.
questions.e: The DICT Act of 2015 created the department.

questions.q: Illegal access is a cybercrime under R.A. 10175.
questions.e: Illegal access is one of the Sec. 4 offenses.

questions.q: Cybersquatting is a [[legal]] business practice under Philippine law.
questions.e: Bad-faith domain acquisition is criminalized.

questions.q: Data subjects have a right to data portability.
questions.e: Portability is among the data subject rights.

questions.q: Sensitive personal information includes health data.
questions.e: Health information is sensitive personal information.

questions.q: A data breach must be reported to the NPC within [[30 days]].
questions.e: The IRR requires notification within 72 hours.

questions.q: R.A. 9775 applies [[only to printed materials]] and not to online content.
questions.fix: to all media, including online content
questions.e: The law covers electronic and digital media.

questions.q: Photo and video voyeurism requires lack of consent and a reasonable expectation of privacy.
questions.e: Both elements are central to the offense.

questions.q: R.A. 10175 [[does not cover]] libel committed online.
questions.e: Cyber libel is explicitly included.

questions.q: Consent under R.A. 10173 may be [[implied from a person's silence]].
questions.e: Silence does not equal valid consent.

questions.q: The DICT is the primary policy and planning agency for ICT in the Philippines.
questions.e: R.A. 10844 established this mandate.
